validation.evidence: 4 recovery files and 27 tests passed across control-plane restart, runtime loss, effect crash boundaries, fencing, reconciliation, and backend continuation.
Format, lint and boundaries, lockfile integrity, immutable image pins, secret scan, typecheck, 91 unit tests, 71 contract tests, and 110 integration tests passed.
19 of 19 Chromium tests passed, including pause, restart, reconnect, recovery progress, backend switch, approval-required replay, and actionable blocked recovery states.
Contract derivatives generated successfully from the approved schemas.
Generated TypeScript derivatives reproduce from the approved OpenAPI and runner protocol contracts.

All five US4 acceptance scenarios, FR-023 through FR-029, FR-035, SC-002, SC-005, and SC-008 align across the specification, plan, tasks, contracts, implementation, tests, and evidence; no task was appended and T069+ was not evaluated as current work.

checkpointEvidence.contract: Versioned, complete, provider-neutral checkpoints are schema-validated, deep-frozen, and integrity-bound by a deterministic SHA-256 material hash.
checkpointEvidence.contents: Objective, acceptance criteria, task state, decisions, open questions, repository and diff state, tool results, artifacts, evidence, remaining work, context manifest, budget, lease, and effect reconciliation state are required reconstruction inputs.
checkpointEvidence.compatibility: Unsupported versions, incomplete state, invalid hashes, corrupt material, missing checkpoints, and sequence gaps fail closed into an actionable recovery block.
checkpointEvidence.backendNeutrality: Provider and harness session identifiers are optional hints only and are excluded from reconstruction authority.

crashBoundaryEvidence.result: Every scripted boundary preserves committed authoritative state and dispatches no recovery-side effect blindly; durable publication and browser delivery converge without a second semantic effect.

fencingEvidence.lossDetection: Durable runtime heartbeats are compared with PostgreSQL authority time, and expired owners are recovered after the configured lease interval.
fencingEvidence.authorityTuple: Effect authority is validated against the exact owner, lease, execution, and fencing-token tuple.
fencingEvidence.successorAuthority: Recovery revokes the old lease and mints a monotonically greater fencing token before successor scheduling.
fencingEvidence.lateSourceRejection: Late calls from the lost runtime are rejected after successor authority is durable.

effectReconciliationEvidence.durablePrepare: Intent, approval, semantic idempotency key, effect identity, and execution authority are committed before remote fixture invocation.
effectReconciliationEvidence.transactionBoundary: Remote continuation and effect lookup execute outside PostgreSQL transactions; durable finalization is replayable with stable identities.
effectReconciliationEvidence.groundTruth: Bounded lookup classifies APPLIED, NOT_APPLIED, or UNKNOWN after revoking lost-runtime authority.
effectReconciliationEvidence.applied: APPLIED resumes only after the effect boundary and records the observed completed result without redispatch.
effectReconciliationEvidence.notApplied: NOT_APPLIED re-plans before the effect; an uncertain prior attempt receives a fresh approval and effect attempt identity while retaining the same semantic key.
effectReconciliationEvidence.unknown: UNKNOWN remains blocked for supervisor attention after bounded lookup rather than retrying blindly.

identityAndBackendEvidence.stableAuthority: Project, task, and specialist identities survive recovery unchanged; a successor execution and runtime receive fresh authority.
identityAndBackendEvidence.route: A second capability-compatible fake connection continues from the compiled provider-neutral checkpoint.
identityAndBackendEvidence.resultValidation: Only a successful CLAIMED_COMPLETE continuation with an APPLIED tool result and deterministic artifact may grant successor continuation authority.
identityAndBackendEvidence.parity: Recovered continuation retains the normalized work hash and deterministic artifact outcome of the uninterrupted fixture journey.

restartAndDeliveryEvidence.reconstruction: PostgreSQL snapshots and ordered durable events reconstruct authoritative identities, approvals, effects, artifacts, evidence, checkpoints, and audit state.
restartAndDeliveryEvidence.queue: Expired queue claims are released, durable lease state is synchronized, and only safe non-paused work is made eligible for successor scheduling.
restartAndDeliveryEvidence.outbox: The production consumer uses claim, projection apply, checkpoint advance, and ACK phases with expired-claim recovery and idempotent replay.
restartAndDeliveryEvidence.projection: Projection checkpoints catch up ordered events without duplicate application after restart or reconnect.
restartAndDeliveryEvidence.safeControlState: PAUSED projects remain paused after restart; missing, corrupt, incompatible, or gapped checkpoint state becomes actionable BLOCKED_RECOVERY.
restartAndDeliveryEvidence.startupFailureIsolation: A missing compatible secondary connection is persisted as BLOCKED_RECOVERY without preventing the control plane from becoming ready.

independentReview.repairs: Review drove separation of backend planning from completion, strict successful-continuation validation, fresh approval after a reconciled non-applied uncertain attempt, fail-closed backend error persistence, and startup isolation when no compatible secondary exists.
independentReview.reviewedRisks: Checkpoint completeness and integrity, restart reconstruction, PostgreSQL outbox recovery, heartbeat expiry, monotonic fencing, stale authority, effect reconciliation, transaction boundaries, semantic replay, backend-switch identity, result truthfulness, browser recovery, scope, and secret safety.
